description: This data set pairs daily COVID-19 hospital and intensive care admissions in France with measures of how people moved and met, to test whether contact networks predict hospital demand. The producer is Christian Selinger of the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (IRD), who used it in a 2021 article in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. Coverage is metropolitan France by département and nationally, daily from 24 March 2020 to 30 March 2021. Columns give hospital admission, intensive care admission, hospital death and discharge incidence, temperature, and quantiles of network measures built from Facebook colocation and Google mobility data, such as clustering, curvature, strength and betweenness within and between départements. The two CSV files are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the network measures are derived from commercial mobility products that are no longer published, variable definitions are in the article, and the hospital series are public health agency counts, not capacity or occupancy. Simulation uses: forecasting hospital and ICU admissions a few weeks ahead to plan surge capacity, and testing how mobility restrictions feed through to hospital load. Related records: CHIME (model-chime) and patientflow (model-patientflow) forecast hospital demand.
name: COVID-19 hospital incidence, temperature and human contact network analytics for France (2020-2021)
